messages:
maria: Alert fired: p99 SLO burn in euw1 hosted-infer (last 10m). probe spike from 0.4% -> 4.8% 5xx. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/euw1/slo?id=svc-hosted-infer :alarm_clock:
ajay: grabbing initial logs. is this from the synthetic probe or real customer traffic?
maria: probe and a small customer complaint (ticket #4328) saying timeouts + 502s. probe and real both trending up.
oncall-bot: [ALERT] SLO_ALERT euw1-hosted-infer p99_latency 2026-03-17T00:12Z -> runbook: https://runbooks.red/hosted-infer-slo
leo: quick query I ran: ```logs.query("env:euw1 service:api-gateway status:[500 TO 599] | count() by verb, status | sort desc")``` seeing a cluster around 502 and 504, a lot on POST /v1/generate. :eyes:
ajay: can we check traces for the 502s? I suspect prefetch/handshake timeouts at ingress -> model pool. jaeger: https://traces.red/trace?q=svc:hosted-infer+status:502
nora: customer repro from support: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -v` — they see socket timeout after ~8s then a 502. token looked valid on their side.
leo: sample logs (redacted): ```[2026-03-17T00:07:45Z] gateway-id=gw-42 req=abc123 status=502 upstream_err="handshake timeout" pool=hosted-infer-pool-A```. Also multiple entries with `kv-cache miss` right before handshake timeout.
maria: interesting, billing shows no usage spike for that customer during the window (billing-service rates low). could be an authz token refresh problem where request body is dropped and gateway retries fail?
ajay: hypothesis: authz middleware stalls on cache misses -> blocks request header read -> upstream handshake times out -> gateway 502. Need trace spans to confirm where time spent.
leo: I increased sampling on gateway->authz for 5 minutes and enabled debug for prefetcher on pool-A. Will revert after 10m. Patch applied: `svc-config set gateway.authz.trace_sampling=1.0`
devex-jess: support note ready for customer: "we're investigating an intermittent ingress timeout impacting a subset of requests, could you share request id if you hit it again?" sending now.
oncall-bot: [ACTION] temporarily routing 10% traffic from pool-A -> pool-B for mitigation. See: https://ops.red/route/detail?id=route-2026-03-17
maria: good temporary mitigation. capture one full trace id that failed after routing change: trace=trc-7ff4b1.
leo: pulled trace trc-7ff4b1: gap between `gateway:receive` and `authz:check` ~6.2s, no downstream spans until handshake timeout. authz service shows repeated cache miss then remote KMS call with 5s tail.
ajay: that KMS call latency ~5s could be root. are we seeing spikes in KMS region? check metrics: `kms.request.latency{region=euw1}` shows 95th=4.9s right now.
maria: if KMS is slow, gateway handshake will hit client timeouts and return 502s. But why probe shows 504s too? maybe batcher/backpressure causing longer queuing.
leo: added a quick log extract for queuing: ```metrics.query("sum(rate(gateway.request.queue_time_seconds[1m])) by (pool)")``` showing pool-A queue_time p95 up 2.1s.
nora: support update: customer provided full request id abc123, attaching to ticket. They also reported client-side retry that doubled traffic briefly.
ajay: immediate next steps: 1) keep mitigation routing 2) escalate KMS latency to infra oncall 3) collect full traces for 30m window 4) check batching backlog and prefetcher thrash 5) reply to customer with repro guidance (no immediate token rotation)
maria: escalation to infra done (pager duty to team-infra). I created a short dashboard with authz span latency + gateway 502 rate: https://dash.red/quick/euw1-authz-gw502
leo: if KMS latency is the offender, long-term fix: add local caching for authz keys + circuit-breaker fallbacks to avoid authz blocking request thread.
devex-jess: drafting customer-facing blurb: "we've routed traffic away from the affected pool and we're investigating an upstream authz dependency causing intermittent timeouts. We'll follow up with root cause."
oncall-bot: [RESOLVE] temporary routing rule will auto-revert 2026-03-17T00:40Z unless extended.
maria: saving logs/trace ids to the incident doc: https://incidents.red/3745001111. Closing thread here, continuing investigation in incident doc. :white_check_mark:
